cards.text: Paul is a prisoner, and his ship just broke apart on a sandbar. Every person on board made it safely to land, some swimming, some floating on planks. The writer traveling with Paul tells this part as "we," and now the whole soggy crew needs to know one thing: WHERE are we?

cards.question: Safely ashore, the shipwrecked crew learns the name of the island they've landed on. What is it?

cards.text: It's raining, it's cold, and a whole shipload of soaking-wet strangers just came up out of the surf. The islanders don't panic. They show "extraordinary kindness."

cards.question: Because it's raining and cold, the islanders kindle a ___ and welcome all of the shipwrecked travelers.

cards.text: The man just survived a shipwreck, and Paul's out gathering a bundle of sticks for the fire. If that were me, I'd be lying flat as a cookie on a cooling rack for a WEEK.

cards.question: As Paul lays his sticks on the fire, the heat drives something out. What fastens itself to Paul's hand?

cards.text: The islanders see the creature hanging from Paul's hand, and they start talking to one another. I bet they're thinking: this man escaped the sea, and NOW this?

cards.question: Seeing the creature hanging from Paul's hand, what do the islanders say Paul surely is?
The islanders say Justice has not allowed Paul to live. Paul shakes the creature off into the fire, and his hand swells up badly.

cards.text: The islanders are expecting Paul to swell up or suddenly drop dead. So they watch him the way I watch a batch through the oven window: nobody blinks, nobody talks, EVERYBODY leaning in.

cards.question: After waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to Paul, the islanders change their minds. What do they say Paul is now?

cards.text: From murderer to god. That's the BIGGEST promotion I have EVER seen. Nearby stands an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island.

cards.question: On his estate, Publius ___ the travelers and entertains them hospitably for ___ days.

cards.text: But there's trouble on the estate: the father of Publius is sick in bed with fever and dysentery. Paul goes in to see him.

cards.question: Paul is at the bedside of Publius's sick father. What does Paul do?

answers.text: He prays and places his hands on him
He anoints him with oil and leaves
He sends for the island's physician

cards.text: And the man is HEALED! On a small island, news like that travels faster than a group text with the word "FREE" in it.

cards.question: After the father of Publius is healed, the rest of the ___ on the island come and are cured as well.

cards.text: The islanders honor Paul and everyone with him in many ways. Remember, these folks started with a fire on a rainy beach, and they just keep on giving.

cards.question: When the travelers are ready to sail, the islanders supply their needs.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave the island for now. Trust me, friend, Paul's voyage isn't over yet.

findings.problem: The card says "Paul is a prisoner," but that fact isn't in Acts 27:41-44. It comes from earlier in the voyage (Acts 27:1). The citation is narrower than what the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The question says Publius "entertains them hospitably." That wording rules out the wrong answers "arrests" and "questions" for the first blank, so the setup gives the answer away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question says "the rest of the ___ on the island come and are cured," following the healing of a sick man. "Cured" and "the rest of" rule out "elders" and "sailors," so the question answers itself.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The line "they just keep on giving" gives away the answer to card 19, which asks whether the islanders supply the travelers' needs.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Acts 28:10 says the islanders "honored us." It doesn't say who "us" includes. The card says "Paul and everyone with him," which decides something the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Card 20 contains only the "story isn't over" line. It retells nothing from the passage, but it cites Acts 28:10, which cards 18 and 19 already cover.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the "story isn't over" line, what should it cite: the passage's last verse, nothing, or something else?
